comparator.name: Cognition, Language and Communication
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current study-programme page specifies a complete 180-EC curriculum. Year 1 is a common 60-EC interdisciplinary foundation. Years 2 and 3 combine a 54-EC CLC core, a 30-EC bound specialisation package drawn from another programme, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor research project. For this generic target, Psychology is selected by the neutral first-listed option on the official programme page before comparison with UCR. The public page publishes that package only as 24 EC of bound choice in Year 2 and 6 EC in Year 3, so those aggregates are preserved rather than populated with invented course names.

core: Cognition, language and communication studied together across humanities, behavioural science and computational science
Empirical inquiry using experimental, qualitative, statistical and computational methods
A disciplinary specialisation, open elective space and a culminating bachelor research project
adjacent: Artificial intelligence, programming and cognitive modelling
Linguistics, psycholinguistics and language learning and use
Communication science, rhetoric, persuasion, social interaction and multimodality
Philosophy, Dutch language and literature, music and cultural expression
questions: How do brain and mind make language, memory, attention and reasoning possible?
How can computational models and artificial intelligence explain or shape cognition and language?
How do rhetoric, persuasion, interaction and communication channels shape mutual understanding?

candidates.label: Language & Communication Studies
candidates.reason: These directions already form the defining language-and-communication spine of the closest match rather than a separate remaining alternative.

candidates.label: Philosophy of Mind & Language
candidates.reason: Coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included.

candidates.label: Music, Cognition & Culture
candidates.reason: Coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included.

alternatives.label: Language, Cognition & Communication
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines cognition and psychology with communication, philosophy, data and computational methods, reflecting all three defining domains rather than reducing CLC to linguistics alone.
alternatives.concept: A broad interdisciplinary pathway joining cognition, language, communication, empirical methods and reflective humanities.
progression: Foundational brain and behaviour, communication, data and social science precede perception, development, higher cognition, psycholinguistics and advanced research. Formal prerequisites and semester availability are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Cognitive Psychology & Neuroscience
alternatives.concept: A brain-and-behaviour direction exploring cognition through psychology, neuroscience, life science and quantitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative replaces most communication, language and humanities breadth with a sustained psychology, neuroscience, life-science and biomedical sequence.
progression: Life-science foundations precede physiology, anatomy and laboratory work, then disease and pathology; cognition, psychology and data courses build from earlier gateways and methods, and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule concentrates on cognitive psychology, brain and behaviour, life science, biomedical study and data methods while retaining the target’s empirical cognition focus.

alternatives.label: Language, Computation & Artificial Intelligence
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule builds a continuous programming, data, mathematics and AI sequence around language, cognition, psychology and communication.
alternatives.concept: A computational direction using programming, data, mathematics and AI to model cognition, language and communication.
progression: Programming, data science and communication precede machine learning, AI, deep learning, optimisation, advanced cognition, psycholinguistics and statistical research. All formal prerequisites and semester offerings are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative replaces most society, media, literature and qualitative breadth with a continuous programming, data, mathematics and artificial-intelligence spine.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the broad CLC programme and does not privilege one bound specialisation. Psychology is the first option listed in the official description of the second-year package and is therefore selected before UCR comparison. The 24-EC and 6-EC aggregates are retained because the public curriculum does not provide a dependable internal course split.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-defining cognition, language, communication and empirical-research interests. Cognitive Psychology & Psychobiology and Artificial Intelligence & Cognitive Modelling are the two strongest coherent remaining generator directions and produce feasible, substantively distinct curricula. Language & Communication Studies is already covered by the closest match. Philosophy of Mind & Language and Music, Cognition & Culture are coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. All three schedules contain 24 courses/180 EC, satisfy prerequisite and term constraints, and provide substantial 300-level depth.

notes.text: CLC combines a common interdisciplinary core, a 30-EC external specialisation package, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor research project. UCR distributes cognate study across a student-designed 24-course Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum.
The selected Psychology package is published only as 24 EC in Year 2 and 6 EC in Year 3. Those aggregates are preserved rather than populated with invented course names or credit allocations.
CLC is bilingual in practice, with Dutch and English courses and materials; UCR’s curriculum is English-taught.
